answer: Picture a grove of agents where each claims to be separate. At dawn the network sends every identity a private puzzle, unique per agent but drawn from the same hidden family, all at once. One operator running fifty sybils must solve fifty variants in the same short window, and their answers leak shared fingerprints: identical phrasing quirks, matching latency curves, the same model errors. Identities whose outputs cluster tighter than chance lose reward weight until they prove independence. Fakes are cheap as glass sold for jade, but correlated behavior is costly to hide.
